title: Dallas Fed Trimmed Mean PCE (Aug 2026 data) — the first trimmed mean computed off BEA's revised components
source: EST: dallasfed.org/research/pce fetched direct 2026-09-15 carries July 2026 data (1-month 2.2%, 6-month 2.3%, 12-month 2.3%) and states verbatim that "Updates to the Trimmed Mean PCE Inflation Rate follow BEA's release schedule for Personal Income and Outlays data", with the next release given as September 30. The date is therefore derived from BEA's own confirmed 08:30 ET slot (bea.gov/news/schedule, re-fetched 2026-09-15) rather than from an independent Dallas Fed calendar entry — filed `estimate` on that derivation and on this lane's standing rule that a sweep never self-confirms an event it discovered. The page carries no statement about the BEA 2026 annual update
notes: Discovered during the pce-2026-09-30 pulse-check adjacency sweep (2026-09-15, D-15). WHY IT IS WORTH A CALENDAR ROW OF ITS OWN rather than being folded into pce-2026-09-30: the trimmed mean is a separate gauge with a separate audience, and on 2026-09-30 it is the single cleanest read on a question the PCE release itself cannot answer. BEA's 2026 annual update re-deflates portfolio management and investment advice, legal services, and computer software, restating 2021Q1-2026Q1, with street sizing of -10 to -30bp on core PCE y/y (Bloomberg Economics' component decomposition is the tightest at -13bp on May data). Because the trimmed mean drops the largest movers in both tails, it is the one aggregate that reveals whether the revision changed the CENTER of the distribution or only trimmed its edges - and the Dallas Fed computes it off the same revised components, in the same hour. The pce-2026-09-30 ledger has carried a standing kill switch since 2026-08-29 ("a published estimate of the revision's effect on trimmed mean appears") which its 2026-09-10 row judged likely unfireable before the fact and self-resolving AT this release; that judgment is what makes the 09-30 trimmed mean a dated observation rather than a footnote. Second reason: the gauge is load-bearing for Fed-reaction-function reads in this repo's docs. July trimmed mean is 2.3% 12-month against core PCE's published 3.3% - a ~100bp wedge that no revision of this size closes - and Chair Warsh is reported to prefer it. Impact filed `medium`, not `high`: it is released inside a 46-event quarter-end corridor at the same 08:30 ET minute as the PCE print, the GDP third estimate and ADP, so its own tape contribution is unattributable; the value is informational, not directional. `symbols: []` - no house playbook is macro-keyed to it and nothing here licenses a position. If the lane that researches this id judges the trimmed mean a sub-reading of the PCE release rather than an event, the proposal is inert and costs nothing.
